authority.rule: When documentation conflicts with current source/runtime behavior, current source wins.

cli.runtimeMode: Use the default JavaScript Runtime. Do not add the compatibility-only -stack flag to new commands.

aiCli.purpose: Low-token desktop tool surface for coding agents; reuses Stable Runtime services and Execution evidence.

runtimeRules: For coding-agent desktop interaction, inspect `opendesk ai schema` and `opendesk ai capabilities`; prefer its window metadata, targeted screenshots, deterministic primitives, and reusable recipes before full-screen visual reasoning.
Prefer stable documented APIs for new scripts.

Treat JavaScript compatibility as a tested feature baseline, not an edition-wide claim. The language gate covers selected ES2015-ES2023 authoring syntax and built-ins; script-level await is provided by the OpenDesk execution wrapper and is not ESM. Static/dynamic ESM loading is unsupported, while require/module/exports are reserved implementation compatibility globals rather than public APIs.
Prefer page.ensurePermissions for permission-gated desktop workflows.
For external desktop UI, prefer UI.findText/UI.tapText and Geometry over direct OCR bbox clicking. Use Vision.runOCR for raw OCR; Vision.detectUI is a deprecated image-local compatibility helper.
Use ImageColor as a secondary pixel/template/color primitive, not as a replacement for semantic verification.

Prefer axios for normal script HTTP requests; axios is a polyfill backed by http.request. Use http.download only for host-authorized native streaming GET downloads; local CLI and ai run enable it, while HTTP, MCP, Scheduler, generic Runtime, JavaScript options, and environment variables cannot grant it.

NativeExtensions is an Experimental manifest-discovered immutable binding. Normal local CLI calls use NativeExtensions.<namespace>.<method>(businessParams) with routes fixed by the Host; it discovers only the program-relative bundle directory by default. HTTP and MCP cannot enable or call it. The low-level NativeExtension.call compatibility surface requires the separate -experimental-unsafe-native-extension-call local diagnostic gate.

Accessibility is an execution-owned Experimental local Runtime API. Trusted local script and AI CLI entrypoints explicitly enable it; HTTP, MCP, Scheduler, and generic Runtime initialization leave it disabled. Every traversal requires an explicit window, execution-owned element ref, or App target scope. It never silently falls back to OCR or mouse input.

Uppercase UI operates visible targets in external desktop apps. Lowercase ui is always present but dormant by default and creates OpenDesk Custom UI; enable it with -ui or strict clawdesk.runtime.json. They have no aliases.

Dialog is always present but fail-closed without the ui capability. Its alert, confirm, and prompt methods are asynchronous native modal dialogs; global alert/confirm/prompt are thin polyfill aliases, never browser-style blocking calls.
Omit -stack for new scripts. The old upgraded/playwright values and browser/context-shaped globals are implementation compatibility residue, not maintained user APIs or a browser engine.

Use the frozen Execution.env snapshot for local project and inherited OS environment values. Local executions merge .env, .opendesk.env, then the environment supplied when the OpenDesk process started; they do not parse shell startup files. Windows names are uppercase. Remote and scheduled executions do not inherit host environment secrets.

Command is an execution-owned native command runner, not Node.js child_process. Local -script and ai run executions enable it by default; HTTP, MCP, and Scheduler executions disable it. Use Command.run(executable,args,options) without shell command interpolation.

SQLite is a first-party, Promise-only local Runtime API, not a Native Extension. Use SQLite.open({path, mode}) and the returned handle's query/exec/batch/close methods with bound parameters; it is enabled only for trusted local script/AI executions and is absent from HTTP, MCP, and Scheduler to avoid granting remote filesystem database access.

Use the native lowercase path global for platform path-string operations. path.resolve and path.relative use the immutable Execution.workdir, not the host process cwd; path never performs filesystem I/O or symlink resolution.
Do not use retired TestMonkey documentation as a current API authority.

globals.name: page
globals.summary: Desktop page entry: screenshot, open URL/App, waits and permissions.
globals.waitSemantics: waitFor dispatches number waits to waitForTimeout and predicates to waitForFunction, forwarding their options. waitForTimeout supports AbortSignal and resolves asynchronously even for 0ms. waitForFunction has an independent deadline and one predicate call in flight; predicate throws/rejections remain transient. waitForAll preserves order, values, identity, and raw rejection reasons, treats functions as values, and never cancels caller-owned work. Duration, timeout, and polling are finite numbers in inclusive 0..86400000; fractional values are accepted and Timer converts them to integer milliseconds. Function/all timeout 0 rejects with TimeoutError/TIMEOUT; signal cancellation rejects with AbortError/CANCELED; invalid arguments use INVALID_ARGUMENT. Every terminal path removes wait-owned timers and listeners.

globals.name: Geometry
globals.coordinateSpace: Consumes WindowInfo, DisplayInfo, or tagged screen regions and emits only tagged virtual-desktop logical screen points/regions. It never accepts a bare bbox as screen coordinates.

globals.name: Accessibility
globals.source: execution-owned native Runtime + macOS AX / Windows UIA backend
globals.authorization: Enabled only by trusted local script and AI CLI execution.Request values. Disabled operations reject without native target reads; getCapabilities remains available and never prompts or crawls the desktop.
globals.capabilities: getCapabilities returns schemaVersion, platform/backend, hostAuthorization.enabled, implementation {available,status,menus,actions,coordinateMapping,notes}, permission {required,state,granted,cached}, top-level available, fixed limits, and cancellation.hardCancel=false. implementation.actions is a per-action boolean map and does not promise element-level support.
globals.scope: Every snapshot/find call requires an existing OpenDeskWindowInfo, an element ref owned by the current execution, or {app: OpenDeskAppTarget, root: application|menuBar}. No implicit whole-desktop traversal.
globals.limits: One total 3000ms default/30000ms maximum deadline including queue time; maxDepth 8/32, maxNodes 1000/5000, 256 active refs, and 32 queued requests per execution.
globals.identity: Element refs are opaque execution-owned objects bound to the process/container/native element. Their public fields cannot be serialized and reconstructed as authority.
globals.actions: invoke, setValue, expand, collapse, select, and setChecked use native capability/state checks and never auto-retry or fall back to pointer input after an attempted action.
globals.lifecycle: Workers, pending/queued requests, refs, and native resources are canceled, joined, counted, and released by the owning execution; hardCancel is false.
globals.coordinates: nativeBounds stays tagged in the backend coordinate space. bounds is null unless a reliable conversion to OpenDesk logical screen coordinates was performed.

globals.name: UI
globals.source: stable visual polyfill plus execution-owned native Accessibility menu composition
globals.coordinateMapping: Every discovery uses a fresh explicit screen clip. imageWidth/logicalScope.width and imageHeight/logicalScope.height are separately calculated actual capture scales; a scope across effective different-DPI displays fails closed.

relativeTextTargeting.requiresWithin: Using region or relativeTo requires an explicit within: OpenDeskWindowInfo so the Runtime can preserve and revalidate window identity.
relativeTextTargeting.region: A tagged OpenDeskScreenRegion snapshot or a synchronous (currentWin: OpenDeskWindowInfo) => OpenDeskScreenRegion rule. Dynamic rules are recomputed once per fresh observation; static regions never track moved windows.
relativeTextTargeting.relativeTo: Uses one exact text anchor from the same capture and Vision.runOCR result. Choose either direction with inclusive maxGap/minOverlap filtering, or a synchronous anchor => tagged screen region whose final intersection must fully contain each target bbox. It never auto-selects the nearest or first candidate.
relativeTextTargeting.spatialUnits: All gaps, overlap calculations, and regions use Geometry desktop logical screen coordinates; never multiply or divide them by Display.scale. Spatial predicates use the continuous logical projection of OCR bboxes before public bounds are outward-rounded; callbacks still receive the public target shape.
relativeTextTargeting.disambiguation: The anchor must be unique and top-level index applies only after target relationship filtering. Missing anchors follow each read method's no-result contract, while clicks fail TARGET_NOT_FOUND with stage=anchor; multiple anchors fail AMBIGUOUS_TARGET with stage=anchor.
relativeTextTargeting.freshness: Revalidate the specified window before capture and after recognition. Dynamic or absent outer regions permit at most one complete pre-input re-observation after same-window bounds changes; static regions fail stale. Never retry after mouse input has been invoked.
relativeTextTargeting.unsupportedBehavior: Passing region or relativeTo to an unsupported method fails with INVALID_ARGUMENT before observation or input. Image and Accessibility anchors are not supported.

menu.scope: Requires a resolved OpenDeskWindowInfo or {app: OpenDeskAppTarget, root: menuBar}; read methods never expand or focus menus.
menu.path: A non-empty complete hierarchy path whose segments are non-empty strings or exact {name?,identifier?} AND selectors.
menu.action: tapMenuItem serially expands freshly observed unique levels under one total deadline, then submits invoke/select/setChecked at most once through the same AccessibilityRuntime.
menu.compatibility: Existing UI text/image methods retain their screenshot, OCR, image and mouse contracts; they are not silently replaced with native Accessibility actions.

globals.name: Events
globals.source: native runtime wrapper + explicit polling backend
globals.notes: Polling is reported in capability and event payloads; no MCP/HTTP surface and no GlobalShortcut duplication. Window events are unsupported on platforms where the existing window facade is unavailable.

globals.name: App
globals.source: native Runtime wrapper + existing NSWorkspace/process/window backends
globals.identity: PID, name, bundleId, or path; stable bundle/path identity is preferred and one identity may group multiple process instances. macOS+cgo recognizes only the exact system aliases 计算器 and Calculator, each normalized to com.apple.calculator; explicit bundleId/path/PID targets and unknown names are never translated
globals.readiness: process or an existing Window-facade row owned by a matching PID; custom predicates are explicitly unsupported
globals.lifecycle: Promise workers are execution-scoped, context-cancelable, timeout-bounded, and joined during Runtime teardown
globals.compatibility: page.openApp and AI CLI app.open retain their public contract while sharing the same launch bridge; System process and Window APIs remain independent
globals.platformBehavior: macOS+cgo uses NSWorkspace/Open/NSRunningApplication and recognizes the documented Calculator aliases through the existing bundle-ID launcher; macOS without cgo and Windows/Linux retain existing name/path behavior without those aliases. Windows/Linux use explicit partial process fallbacks and are not live verified
globals.surface: JavaScript Runtime only in this phase; no HTTP or MCP method was added

globals.name: Notifications
globals.source: execution-owned Runtime wrapper + macOS UserNotifications own-app model
globals.scope: macOS lists and removes only notifications delivered by the OpenDesk app identity; arbitrary application notifications are not exposed
globals.privacy: title and message are redacted by default and require includeContent=true; metadata stays scoped to OpenDesk
globals.identity: opaque UserNotifications request identifier plus OpenDesk app identity and delivery timestamp; duplicate content is not treated as identity
globals.lifecycle: waitFor uses a bounded own-app poll, prefers new notifications by default, runs under the execution context, and is canceled and joined during teardown
globals.unsupported: activate is not exposed because public UserNotifications APIs report user actions but cannot simulate them; Events does not claim notification.changed
globals.platformBehavior: Windows UserNotificationListener requires manifest capability, package/app identity, and user consent not present in the current OpenDesk host; Linux has no equivalent stable unified backend. Both fail closed.
globals.surface: JavaScript Runtime only; outbound sending remains the existing notify() global

globals.name: window
globals.source: native facade + CoreGraphics/System Events or Win32 backend + normalization polyfill
globals.identity: Every observed row has an id. A uniquely resolved row uses platform:pid:native:nativeHandle; metadata-poor or cross-Space rows use platform:pid:unresolved and must not be treated as stable. Title actions resolve a unique current title first and reject duplicate titles.
globals.coordinateSpace: macOS uses global display points with a primary-display top-left origin and possible negative secondary coordinates; Windows uses virtual-screen logical coordinates subject to DPI awareness.
globals.staleTarget: A title action that resolves successfully but loses or renames its target before the backend action reports STALE_TARGET. Initial absence reports NOT_FOUND.
globals.platformBehavior: macOS core paths are live fixture-verified but arbitrary actions remain permission/app/Space dependent; Windows source is target-compiled but not live verified in this macOS evidence run; Linux is explicit Unsupported.
globals.surface: The existing JavaScript window facade was extended; no second backend, HTTP route, MCP tool, Accessibility tree, or Spaces manager was added.

globals.name: Screen
globals.notes: Display inventory, pixel, and screenshot methods remain stable. Existing Screen owns display inventory; no duplicate Display global was added. macOS CoreGraphics mode read/list are available and setDisplayMode is Experimental with synchronous readback and caller restore. Brightness is explicitly Unsupported and delegated to hardware-specific Native Extensions. selectRegion/startRecording are Experimental on macOS; audio and frame streaming are explicitly unavailable.

globals.name: System
globals.source: native + execution environment adapter + platform session backend
globals.status: stable reads with experimental session actions
globals.sessionSafety: lock, logout, and startScreenSaver require confirm=true before backend access; success returns initiated=true and verified=false because request acceptance is not a postcondition
globals.environmentAccess: getEnv(name, optionalFallback) and hasEnv(name) read only the same per-execution snapshot exposed by Execution.env. They never refresh os.Environ or bypass the empty remote/scheduled environment, and no getAllEnv method is exposed.
globals.sessionIdentity: getSessionState returns only normalized user/session identity and state; unavailable booleans including locked are null rather than inferred
globals.platformBehavior: macOS public CGSessionCopyCurrentDictionary supports read-only WindowServer session state and leaves locked unknown; ScreenSaverEngine launch is Experimental while lock/logout are unsupported. Windows uses public LockWorkStation/ExitWindowsEx candidates but remains target-runtime unverified. Linux requires loginctl plus XDG_SESSION_ID and remains target-runtime unverified.
globals.compatibility: existing shutdown, restart, and sleep remain the separate legacy power-control surface; this task does not create a second System or Power namespace

globals.name: Execution
globals.lifecycle: Read-only per-execution context contract; it does not create, cancel, pause, resume, or enumerate executions.
globals.environment: env is a frozen string snapshot. Trusted local -script and ai run executions merge .env, .opendesk.env (or one explicit env file), then the OS environment supplied when OpenDesk started; no login shell or startup file is parsed. Windows names are canonical uppercase. HTTP, MCP, and Scheduler executions receive an empty snapshot by default.
globals.sourcePath: scriptPath is a normalized absolute trusted file path and scriptDir is its parent. Direct -script, ai run, and Scheduler file executions provide them; inline, stdin, HTTP, MCP, and Scheduler inline executions expose null. They are never parsed from source labels.
globals.privacy: env may contain credentials and source/workdir/scriptPath may contain local paths; do not serialize them into logs or remote requests. scriptHash is a correlation aid, not a signature or trust decision.

globals.name: Command
globals.source: native execution owner + platform process-group adapter
globals.availability: Enabled by default for local -script and ai run executions. Disabled for HTTP, MCP, and Scheduler executions.
globals.signature: Command.run(command, args?, {cwd?, env?, input?, timeout?, maxOutputBytes?}) -> Promise<{exitCode,stdout,stderr}>
globals.capabilities: getCapabilities returns only schemaVersion=1, enabled, supported, and executionScoped=true.
globals.errors: CommandError exposes name, code, exitCode, stdout, and stderr.
globals.safety: run executes an executable directly with an optional argument array. Combined stdout/stderr is bounded; shell interpretation, streaming handles, detached/unref, IPC, and PTY are not exposed.
globals.lifecycle: The enclosing execution stays alive while a command runs, and teardown terminates remaining command processes.

globals.name: path
globals.source: native path-string helper backed by the execution File WorkDir
globals.compatibility: Common string behavior tracks Node.js 24.15.0 node:path on the target platform. OpenDesk intentionally uses Execution.workdir instead of process.cwd for resolve and relative.
globals.safety: String-only and synchronous: no disk access, existence checks, symlink resolution, tilde/environment expansion, process cwd mutation, or lifecycle resources.

globals.name: File
globals.workdir: File.cwd and every relative File path use the normalized Execution.workdir for this execution.
globals.open: File.open returns a constrained synchronous FileHandle (close, read/readBytes, write/writeBytes, seek, truncate, sync), never a raw host file descriptor. Runtime teardown closes unclosed handles.
globals.json: readJSON and writeJSON are Promise-based; JSON uses Runtime JSON.parse/stringify semantics, has an 8 MiB maximum per operation and 128 container nesting limit.
globals.writeSafety: writeJSON uses a supported same-directory replacement backend on macOS/Linux. Windows fails closed with ATOMIC_REPLACE_UNSUPPORTED; it never truncates as a fallback.

globals.name: SQLite
globals.availability: Injected only for trusted local -script, -script-text, -script-stdin, and ai run executions. HTTP, MCP, and Scheduler do not inject SQLite and no generic SQL route/tool is added.
globals.pathResolution: Relative paths use immutable Execution.workdir exactly like File.path. rw is the default and opens an existing file only; rwc permits file creation but never creates parent directories; ro is enforced at SQLite connection level. POSIX backslashes stay literal filename characters; Windows paths use Windows separator/drive/UNC rules. :memory: is isolated per handle and rejects ro. Protected Scheduler database paths (default and direct CLI -scheduler-db) reject PROTECTED_PATH, including resolvable symlink aliases.
globals.values: Parameters use real SQLite binding: sequential ? arrays or exact named parameter objects (names start with a Unicode letter and may then contain letters/digits/_), with null/boolean/string/finite number/SQLite-range BigInt/Uint8Array. BLOB input snapshots before enqueue; unsafe INTEGER output is exact decimal text and BLOB output is Uint8Array.
globals.queryLimits: query defaults to 10000 rows and 8 MiB, configurable up to 100000 rows and 64 MiB; it rejects RESULT_LIMIT instead of truncating. query is not a read-only guarantee: DML RETURNING may write, and a limit/cancel/read error there can report writeState unknown/committed null.
globals.transaction: batch({sql, params?}[]) runs at most 256 single top-level statements in one physical-connection transaction; all success commits, and failure/cancel before commit rolls back. A commit-race error reports writeState unknown/committed null and must not be automatically retried. Raw transaction and connection-changing SQL are rejected.
globals.lifecycle: Each handle has a bounded serialized queue, operation context/timeout/AbortSignal, and an execution-owned worker. close fences new work and waits prior accepted work; execution teardown cancels and releases forgotten handles. SQLiteError carries code, operation, committed, and writeState including unknown outcomes that must not be automatically retried.

globals.name: clipboard
globals.capability: Stable text compatibility API on all supported desktops; experimental rich text, PNG, and file representations currently use NSPasteboard on macOS. clipboard.write verifies every requested representation, clipboard.read returns a changeCount-consistent snapshot, and formats:[] reads metadata only. Binary values are canonical base64, files are absolute paths, and Events clipboard.changed reports metadata only.

globals.name: NativeExtensions
globals.source: strict manifest registry plus host-generated immutable binding
globals.condition: available to local CLI JavaScript by default after a complete source-free bundle is installed beside the actual executable; the -script path does not affect discovery; HTTP, MCP, and other remote execution transports never inject, enable, redirect, or call it
globals.summary: Discovers strict extension.json bundles from exactly one portable/app-bundled program-relative root; it does not compile or install source examples, generates frozen namespaces and method closures, and starts one validated executable only when a generated method is called.
globals.platformStatus: V1 has Darwin/Linux/Windows implementation candidates; macOS-only examples or Runtime Evidence do not mean the whole API is macOS-only. go-basic is target-buildable Go; macos-vision is macOS-only. A target without target-machine Runtime Evidence is Not Evaluated, not Unsupported.
globals.migration: legacy prototype roots are not scanned or auto-moved/copied/merged/deleted
globals.lifecycle: registry frozen per execution; start a new execution after install or upgrade; no hot reload
globals.errorModel: method failure throws NativeExtensionsError; successful calls return the extension result directly
doesNotExecute: third-party JavaScript facade files during discovery

globals.name: notify
globals.signature: notify(message: string): void; notify(options: OpenDeskNotifyOptions): void
globals.timeout: accepted for compatibility but ignored by current platform notification backends
globals.result: undefined on backend submission success; throws on invalid input or backend failure
globals.validation: options fields use their documented primitive types; timeout must be finite; title and message must be valid UTF-8 without NUL
globals.macOSBackend: native UserNotifications with OpenDesk.app identity; plain CLI and Scheduler re-enter the sibling OpenDesk.app notification-only helper and never use ScriptEditor2/osascript; missing app identity, denied alerts, timeout, helper stderr/exit, and request submission failures throw
globals.sound: sound=true requests the platform default sound; actual sound remains subject to macOS and user settings
globals.visibility: success means NotificationCenter accepted the request after authorization checks; Focus/Do Not Disturb, display sharing/mirroring, and other OS policy may still suppress user-visible presentation

globals.name: Dialog
globals.source: host-owned native binding plus thin polyfill aliases
globals.condition: always injected but DIALOG_DISABLED without the ui capability; CLI needs -ui or trusted config, HTTP additionally needs server enablement, per-request ui and loopback source; Scheduler and MCP have no Dialog opt-in
globals.platformBehavior: macOS normal AppKit top-level window through the existing Custom UI native host; unsupported platforms reject DIALOG_UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM
globals.asyncControlFlow: Promise-only: no onConfirm/onCancel options callbacks and no synchronous EventLoop blocking. await pauses only its async flow; then/catch/finally run on the owner EventLoop. An unobserved Dialog Promise is closed during execution teardown rather than retaining the execution indefinitely; all competing terminal paths settle exactly once.
globals.promptResult: prompt resolves a string on confirm and null on user cancellation. Public examples display a non-sensitive result in a following Dialog.alert; secure or otherwise sensitive input must not be echoed to logs, notifications, or another Dialog.
globals.privacy: secure prompt uses a password input; Dialog never writes message, defaultValue, or prompt input to ordinary logs, errors, summaries, events, or HTTP responses

globals.name: Audio
globals.source: native runtime wrapper + macOS CoreAudio HAL controls + audio pattern matcher/backend seam
globals.capture: not implemented; microphone and systemAudio are explicitly false in capability discovery
globals.patternWatch: experimental contract and bounded in-memory matcher; the default product build currently has no platform capture backend, reports unsupported, and rejects watchSound/waitForSound with NOT_SUPPORTED; source is explicit, raw PCM is neither exposed nor persisted, and a future match is a heuristic wake-up signal rather than a business event
globals.soundCompatibility: Sound keeps blocking MP3/WAV compatibility methods and adds execution-scoped controllable playback sessions
globals.platformBehavior: darwin+cgo uses CoreAudio; non-CGO macOS and other platforms report unavailable and reject instead of silent no-op

globals.name: ui
globals.source: native process driver plus EventLoop bridge
globals.condition: always present but dormant by default; local CLI or strict project config authorization is required, while HTTP additionally requires server opt-in, per-request capability declaration, and a loopback peer; new initial positioning is the discriminated position union {mode:absolute,bounds} or {mode:anchor,size,horizontal,vertical}; established absolute bounds remains a compatibility spelling, while the retired top-level size plus placement draft is rejected; WindowHandle placement composes left/center/right with top/center/bottom inside the selected display work area
globals.platformBehavior: macOS AppKit/WebKit host; Windows and Linux report available=false and createWindow rejects UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM

globals.name: FloatingWindow
globals.source: compact native action-toolbar facade over the Custom UI driver
globals.condition: injected only when Custom UI is explicitly authorized; new initial positioning is the discriminated position union {mode:absolute,x,y} or {mode:anchor,horizontal,vertical}; established paired x/y and the no-position 100/100 default remain compatible, while the retired top-level placement draft is rejected; anchor uses the selected display work area. The typed, versioned ToolbarSpec contains ordered Button, Separator, and fixed Spacer items: horizontal has 1-32 actionable buttons and at most 63 total items, while vertical has 1-5 actionable buttons and at most 9 total items. Button icons accept a reviewed built-in name or {path,renderingMode?} for a script-contained PNG/JPEG; the Runtime rejects URLs, traversal, symlink escape, invalid format/dimensions and resource overflow, then sends only bounded raster data to a host that validates it again. Structural items never receive callbacks, state, focus, or button Accessibility exposure; at a natural wrap boundary they are omitted instead of becoming row-edge artifacts. FloatingWindow remains icon-first: visible group titles, forms, arbitrary layout, flexible spacing and badges are not supported. It reuses shared WindowState, move/close lifecycle events and native draggable readback; conflicting or incomplete positioning, invalid icon declarations, invalid structure/layout constraints, unknown item type and overflow are INVALID_SPEC

globals.name: Global APIs
globals.summary: 无需 import 即可直接调用的计时器、等待、console 日志、剪贴板快捷函数、取消控制、通知与 URL 参数接口。
